How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

Below is a complete, ready‑to‑use RESTful API request that you can copy‑paste into a terminal (curl) or into your preferred HTTP client (Postman, Insomnia, etc.). The request follows the **Cisco Nexus Dashboard** API specification you mentioned: | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Base URL** | `https://192.168.11.33` | | **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes` | | **Query Parameter** | `fabricName=PEK-ACI` | | **Full URL** | `https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI` | | **Headers** | `Accept: application/json`
`Content-Type: application/json`
*(plus any auth header you use – see below)* | | **Authentication** | Typically Basic Auth (`Authorization: Basic `) or a bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer `). Replace with your actual credentials. | --- ### 1. Using `curl` ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -u ":" # <-- Basic Auth # OR # -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` > **Tip:** If you’re on Windows PowerShell, escape the double quotes or use single quotes around the URL. --- ### 2. Using Postman / Insomnia 1. **Method:** `GET` 2. **URL:** `https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI` 3. **Headers:** - `Accept: application/json` - `Content-Type: application/json` - `Authorization: Basic ` *(or Bearer token)* 4. **Body:** *None* (GET request) --- ### 3. Using the provided `requests_get` function (Python) If you prefer to invoke the helper function you supplied, here’s how you’d call it: ```python from functions import requests_get response = requests_get( url="https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}", fabricName="PEK-ACI" ) print(response) ``` > **Note:** The function will internally replace `{fabricName}` with `"PEK-ACI"` and perform the GET request. Make sure the function has access to the necessary authentication context (e.g., a session with the proper headers). --- ### 4. Quick sanity check After sending the request, you should receive a JSON payload similar to: ```json { "nodes": [ { "nodeId": "node-01", "status": "active", "fabricName": "PEK-ACI", ... }, ... ] } ``` If you encounter any errors (e.g., 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found), double‑check: - The IP address and port (default HTTPS 443). - The exact endpoint path (`/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes`). - Your authentication credentials or token. - That the fabric name `PEK-ACI` exists in the system. --- #### Recap - **Method:** GET - **URL:** `https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI` - **Headers:** Accept & Content-Type set to `application/json`; add your auth header. - **Body:** None. Feel free to copy the curl command or the Python snippet directly into your environment. Let me know if you need help with authentication tokens, handling SSL verification, or parsing the response!
